original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Classify arbitrary-coefficient mixed-direction restoring four-shear loops on two dirty roots for M=[[1,1,1],[1,1,-1],[1,-1,0]] with exactly twelve ordinary signed Ai/Bj queries, and settle whether their port tariffs can differ from the existing one-way class.
scope_change_reason: The additional operation is the reverse-direction shear. PR1675 excludes at most three transfers and explicitly leaves four open; PR1682 and the merged nonunit-signed-connector-rigidity theorem only cover one-way four-transfer words. This is a new alphabet classification, not an enlarged coefficient box.
bottleneck_link: The missing mixed-direction classification determines whether four-pass recursive connectors can move expensive child invocations to cheaper ports. No native supplier or kappa improvement is inferred.
stop_rule: First classify every root-only identity symbolically and test its smallest paired-query endpoint. Complete the reduced exact domain, or retain only a precisely proved scope. Do not perform an unbounded coefficient sweep or construct a supplier when the favorable tariff is already impossible.
evidence: README.md Sections 1-3 give the unbounded coefficient reduction and complete exceptional census. EVIDENCE.json binds 69948 canonical source traces, all eight source-sign choices, full reader masks, symbolic identities, source-bound witness controls and exact dirty-state checks. VERIFY.json registers source/certificate corruption and relocated optimized replay.
author: Adam Gall, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for mathematics, implementation, exact experiments and writing. No subagents or independent human review.
method_domain: Two arbitrary dirty roots over Q or C; four nonzero fixed scalar shears of either direction, twelve ordinary +/-1 complete queries, arbitrary fixed linear maps, immutable sources, unread outputs, full restoration. Symbolic root matrices before any finite search.
optimistic_full_budget: I+P+D plus the twelve actual signed fixed-port child prices and four complete full-row shear prices. A port improvement must beat the existing one-way forced-port sum after all routing, coefficient arithmetic, restoration, scratch, precision, admission and dispatch; none is free. This is an abstract-interface target, not a moment change.
success_or_falsification: An exact mixed-direction word for M with a full invoice, or an arbitrary-coefficient impossibility proof for mixed four-shear words and its implication for the complete additive tariff.
